dynamics-365-fraud-protection.title: What is a fraud prevention service? – Microsoft Dynamics 365
dynamics-365-fraud-protection.notes: Dynamics 365 Fraud Protection is described by Microsoft as an AI-driven business solution that targets payment fraud, bot activity and account takeovers. It relies on machine learning, automated processes and analysis of large data volumes, and it learns continuously instead of depending on fixed rules. The product is organized into three areas. Purchase Protection safeguards online revenue, aims at higher bank acceptance and reduces friction at checkout. Account Protection addresses unauthorized account access, fake account creation and takeovers. Loss Prevention supports store managers and investigators in spotting fraud around returns and discounts in omnichannel purchases. Typical use cases are retail and e-commerce settings, covering identity theft, card-not-present fraud, click-and-collect fraud, card testing, cross-channel fraud and mobile payment fraud. The page names integration with existing systems, reporting, customer experience and technical support as evaluation criteria for such solutions. It gives no licensing, pricing or technical prerequisites and lists no product limitations; its performance claims are the vendor's own statements.

dynamics-365-warehouse-management.title: Warehouse management overview – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-warehouse-management.notes: Warehouse management in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management controls how goods move through a warehouse from receiving at the dock to shipping. It assigns tasks to workers, tracks inventory down to location and license plate, and links the warehouse to sales, purchasing, production, quality and transportation. The processes are switched on per warehouse with the option for using warehouse management processes. The warehouse is modeled with zone groups, zones, location profiles, location types and locations. Work templates define which work is created, and location directives define which locations that work uses; both are driven by query-based rules. Further areas include inbound handling with putaway, outbound handling with waves, picking and packing, replenishment, cycle counting, a configurable mobile app with scanning, and an interface for material handling equipment. A separate warehouse management only mode lets a legal entity run warehouse processes alongside an external ERP, for example for third-party logistics. The page lists no licensing details. Limits noted include the lighter feature set of Inventory management, freight planning being handled by Transportation management, and a spatial location feature that is still in preview.

easy-auth.title: Authentication and authorization in Azure App Service and Azure Functions – Microsoft Learn
easy-auth.notes: Easy Auth is the built-in authentication and authorization capability of Azure App Service and Azure Functions. It lets users sign in and reach protected data in web apps, REST APIs, mobile backends and functions with little or no application code. Supported providers include Microsoft Entra, Facebook, Google, X, GitHub, Apple (preview) and any OpenID Connect provider, each with a login endpoint under the .auth path. The feature acts as middleware: it authenticates users and clients, validates, stores and refreshes tokens, manages sessions and passes identity details to the app in HTTP headers. A token store keeps ID, access and refresh tokens per signed-in session. On Windows it runs as native IIS modules, while on Linux and containers it runs in a separate container following the ambassador pattern. Configuration happens through Azure Resource Manager or a file. An app registration at the provider is required, and a client secret is needed for confidential-client behavior. By default it only authenticates, so the application must still make authorization decisions. Requiring authentication applies to the whole app, which means excluded paths need extra configuration. With Azure Front Door, caching for the auth workflow should be turned off.

ediscovery-review-sets.title: Manage review sets in eDiscovery (Premium) – Microsoft Learn
ediscovery-review-sets.notes: A review set in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is a static collection of documents in which case data can be analyzed, queried, viewed, tagged and exported. All review sets of a case are listed on the Review sets tab, which shows details such as size, creator, last modification, related searches and exports, and can be exported as a list. Inside a review set, the All items tab supports searching with a condition builder, with KQL queries in the advanced review set explorer (preview), grouping and viewing items, tagging, running analytics, exporting items and adding items to another review set. A query report for keyword queries is available as a preview. The overview presents counts of extracted documents, processed items and failed extractions, and a preview dashboard shows charts such as top communication participants, data sources, item classes and file extensions. Pagination shows a fixed number of items per page by default and can be turned off. A process manager logs actions such as exports. Items cannot be deleted from a review set, and review sets cannot be deleted from a case; removing one with its data requires deleting the whole case. Cases in limited format use the older interface with fewer functions. The page does not state license requirements.

email-to-case.title: Automatically create or update records – Dynamics 365 Customer Service
email-to-case.notes: Automatic record creation and update rules in Dynamics 365 Customer Service create or update records in Dataverse from incoming activities such as emails, social activities and custom activities. The best-known case is creating support cases from emails sent to a queue. A rule contains one or more rule items, and each item defines conditions and the actions to take. Items are checked in the listed order, and once one matches and creates a case, the remaining items are not evaluated. Supported activities include email, social activity, task, phone call, appointment, service activity and custom activity, and the target can be a standard or custom table such as lead, opportunity or case. Rules are configured in the Copilot Service admin center under case settings, conditions are built in a condition builder, and an optional email template can serve as an automatic reply. Advanced settings cover unknown senders, a required entitlement, a wait period after the linked case is resolved and the rule owner. For email, a queue must be selected before the rule can be activated. Limits include no support for on-premises environments, no automatic reopening of resolved cases, and restrictions on mixing single-queue and multiple-queue rules. Specific licenses are not named.

enterprise-data-protection.title: Microsoft Copilot privacy and protections – Microsoft Learn
enterprise-data-protection.notes: Enterprise data protection, or EDP, is a set of controls and commitments from the Data Protection Addendum and Product Terms that apply to customer data of people using Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat, with Microsoft acting as data processor. Prompts and responses are handled inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary and are not used to train the underlying foundation models. Prompts and responses are logged in Exchange for auditing and eDiscovery, uploaded files go to the user's OneDrive for Business, and Microsoft Purview retention policies and audit logging can be applied. A green shield in the chat interface indicates that protection is active. EDP is available in Copilot Chat at no additional cost, though concrete controls depend on the subscription plan. By default Copilot Chat is grounded only in web data, and organizational content is used only in specific scenarios such as uploaded files or Copilot Chat in Outlook. Web search queries generated by the chat fall outside EDP and are governed by the Microsoft Services Agreement and privacy statement, with Microsoft acting as independent controller. Those Bing queries are also not covered by the EU Data Boundary, while LLM traffic from the EU stays within it.

environment-routing.title: Environment routing – Power Platform admin | Microsoft Learn
environment-routing.notes: Environment routing is a Power Platform governance feature that sends makers to their own personal developer environment when they open Copilot Studio, Power Apps, Power Automate or Power Automate for Desktop, instead of working in the default or a shared environment. It is off by default and is enabled by a tenant admin in the Power Platform admin center, where the admin also chooses the portals that take part. Rules apply to everyone or to selected security groups and assign an environment group whose rules the new environments inherit. Rules are evaluated by priority and the first match wins; if no rule matches, the feature is off or creation fails, the maker lands in the default environment. Existing own developer environments are reused, and makers receive the system administrator role in them. The created environments are managed environments by default, so building and testing needs no premium license but running does. Preconfigured settings include sharing limits, solution checker set to warn and usage insights turned on. Power Pages is not supported, and makers can still switch to other environments afterwards.

event-based-retention.title: Start retention when an event occurs – Microsoft Purview
event-based-retention.notes: Event-based retention in Microsoft Purview lets a retention label start its retention period from a specific event instead of from creation or modification date. It is mainly used in records management, for example keeping employee records for a set period after departure or contracts after they end. The setup has several parts. An event type describes a general kind of event, and a retention label is linked to that type. An asset ID, stored as a property on SharePoint and OneDrive items, or keywords for Exchange items identify the content concerned. An event, created in the Purview portal under records management, carries the event type, optional asset ID or keywords, and the event date. After creation the date is synchronized to matching labeled content, which can take up to seven days. Without an asset ID or keywords, the event affects all content with labels of that type. Records whose event has not occurred are retained indefinitely, and a disposition review is often triggered at the end of the period. The label's event type cannot be changed after saving, and a triggered event cannot be canceled. The older REST APIs no longer work, so Microsoft Graph or PowerShell is used for automation. License requirements are not stated.

expression-trees.title: Expression Trees – C# | Microsoft Learn
expression-trees.notes: Expression trees represent code as a tree-shaped data structure in which every node is an expression, such as a method call or a binary operation like a comparison. They allow code to be inspected, modified or executed at run time, which makes dynamic changes to executable code and dynamic queries possible. Entity Framework uses them to translate LINQ queries into SQL, and the Moq mocking framework and the Dynamic Language Runtime also rely on them. The C# or Visual Basic compiler creates an expression tree when a lambda expression is assigned to a variable of type Expression of a delegate type. Trees can also be built by hand with the System.Linq.Expressions namespace. They are immutable, so a change means building a new tree by copying nodes and replacing parts, and an expression tree visitor is used to walk through a tree. A tree can be compiled and run. Only expression lambdas are supported, not statement lambdas. Many language features cannot appear in them, including await, async lambdas, assignments, dynamic operations, pattern matching, interpolated strings, ref parameters and named or optional arguments. The page recommends prior knowledge of LINQ and lambda expressions and names no license requirements.

fabric-copy-job.title: What is Copy job in Data Factory – Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
fabric-copy-job.notes: Copy job in Microsoft Fabric Data Factory is a way to move data from many sources to many destinations without building pipelines. It supports full copy, where every run copies everything, and incremental copy, where the first run is complete and later runs transfer only new or changed data. Incremental loading works either with a watermark column or with change data capture, and the latter also replicates deletes when it is enabled on the source. Update methods include append, merge, overwrite and slowly changing dimension type 2. Destination tables can be created automatically, truncation before a full load is optional, and audit columns can record details such as extraction time, source file path and run identifiers. Runs can be one-time or scheduled, with several schedules per job, and a copy job can be used as an activity inside pipelines. Gateways handle sources behind firewalls or in virtual networks, Git and CI/CD are supported, and results are monitored in the job view or workspace monitoring. Limits include support for tabular data only, no deletes captured by watermark loading, auto-partitioning and some destinations still in preview, and no deletion in the destination unless truncate is chosen. Specific license terms are not given.

fabric-deployment-pipelines.title: Introduction to deployment pipelines – Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
fabric-deployment-pipelines.notes: Deployment pipelines are the application lifecycle management tool in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. They let creators develop and test content in the service before users reach it, moving it through separate stages. A pipeline has between two and ten stages and by default uses development, test and production, which can be renamed, added or removed. A deployment copies content from one stage to the next and overwrites paired items in the target, while items missing in the source stay untouched in the target. Items in neighboring stages are paired when a workspace is assigned or a clean deploy runs, and the pairing survives renames. The folder structure is carried over. An optional deployment plan, still in preview, sets the order and actions before or after a deployment, and deployments can be automated through REST APIs. Supported item types span lakehouses, notebooks, pipelines, warehouses, reports, semantic models, eventhouses and more, some of them in preview. Items added after workspace assignment are not paired automatically and may produce duplicates, at least one item must be selected, and some item properties are not copied. Version control is the job of Git integration. No license requirements appear on the page.

fabric-tenant-settings.title: About tenant settings – Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
fabric-tenant-settings.notes: Fabric tenant settings are switches that administrators use to decide which features are available in the organization, with fine-grained control. They help when concerns about sensitive data call for restricting a capability, and a feature can be offered to a specific group only. A setting can be disabled for everyone, enabled for everyone, enabled for everyone except named groups, enabled only for selected security groups, or enabled for selected groups with exceptions; when settings conflict, the most restrictive one applies to the user. Administrators open the settings through the OneLake catalog Govern tab or, during regional rollout, through the admin portal, and an index in the documentation lists every setting with a short description. New or changed settings are flagged on the page, and settings can also be read through the Fabric REST API. Access requires signing in to Fabric with an admin account, and no license requirements are given. Settings that govern Power BI interface features are explicitly not a security measure; for example, turning off data export does not remove the ability of someone with read access to a semantic model to query it and save results. The OneLake catalog Govern tab is rolled out by region and is not available everywhere.

flex-consumption-plan.title: Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan hosting | Microsoft Learn
flex-consumption-plan.notes: Flex Consumption is a Linux-based hosting plan for Azure Functions that extends the pay-for-what-you-use serverless model and is described as the recommended serverless plan. Compared with Consumption it adds virtual network integration, a choice of instance memory size and fast, large scale-out. It scales to zero, scales on events, supports optional always-ready instances to reduce cold starts, and scales groups of functions independently, for example HTTP, blob and Durable Functions groups. Instance sizes come in three memory and CPU options. Billing in on-demand mode depends on execution time in GB-seconds and execution count, while always-ready instances add a baseline charge for provisioned memory. Supported stacks include .NET isolated worker, Python, Node.js, Java, PowerShell, Go and custom handlers, and deployment uses a zip package in a blob container. Prerequisites for networking include registering the Microsoft.App resource provider and delegating a subnet. Limits include one app per plan, Linux only, no deployment slots, no in-place migration from other plans, no NFS, blob triggers only via Event Grid, a fixed host initialization timeout, regional quotas on cores and availability in only some regions. No separate license is mentioned.

github-copilot-for-azure.title: What is GitHub Copilot for Azure? – Microsoft Learn
github-copilot-for-azure.notes: GitHub Copilot for Azure is an extension for GitHub Copilot that lets developers use natural language to learn about Azure, deploy resources, retrieve information about resources and diagnose or fix problems. It adds to the general knowledge of large language models by calling tools through the Azure MCP Server, which talks to Azure services and Azure Resource Graph, and it installs Azure Skills for structured, multi-step workflows such as preparing, validating and deploying. It is available in Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio 2026, JetBrains IDEs and Claude Code, and in public preview for Visual Studio 2022. Typical scenarios are learning from Microsoft Learn content, designing and building cloud apps, creating resources and pipelines or removing projects with azd, and troubleshooting causes such as quota consumption, slow Kubernetes clusters or HTTP 500 errors. It needs both an Azure subscription and a GitHub Copilot subscription, and tool availability follows the user's Azure permissions. Limits and cautions: answers must be checked for correctness, cost and security, secrets must not be placed in code or prompts, a prompt must mention Azure so the Azure tools get called, and the page recommends telling the assistant not to act before approval in agent mode.

glossary-term.title: Glossary terms – Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog | Microsoft Learn
glossary-term.notes: A glossary term in the Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog is a single concept that describes the business, its processes and its systems. The page calls terms active values that give context and apply policies governing how data is managed, secured and discovered. Linking a technically named SQL table to a term such as Account makes the data understandable to business users who search in familiar language. Terms are created under governance domains so that the same word can be kept apart per area, for instance sales versus marketing. They can be related to each other and linked to data products, data assets, columns and critical data elements. A term can carry policies, such as data quality goals, governance requirements and terms of use, which are inherited automatically by everything it is linked to. A data steward defines the term once, instead of applying policies to each object separately. Classic glossary terms can be brought into the Unified Catalog and linked to assets and columns, which is a preview capability. The page states no license requirements. It warns that the Unified Catalog and classic data governance in Purview are being retired, that new accounts can no longer be created and that existing features stay in maintenance mode until 12 November 2027.

hierarchical-partition-keys.title: Hierarchical partition keys in Azure Cosmos DB | Microsoft Learn
hierarchical-partition-keys.notes: Hierarchical partition keys, also called subpartitioning, let an Azure Cosmos DB container use a partition key with up to three levels, such as tenant, user and session. They allow data to grow beyond the limit of a single logical partition, because key prefixes can exceed it, and queries that supply a prefix are routed only to the physical partitions that hold the data. A tenant can be mapped to its own logical partition. The item ID can be added as a final level to guarantee scaling. Routing differs by query: a full key hits one partition, a prefix is a targeted cross-partition query, and a missing leading level causes a fan-out across all partitions. Physical partitions split automatically when they grow large enough. The feature is available only for the API for NoSQL, not for MongoDB or Cassandra, and needs supported SDK versions for .NET, Java, JavaScript and Python. It suits multi-tenant apps with large and small tenants, write-heavy workloads with high first-level cardinality and reads that filter on key prefixes. Limits: the hierarchy can only be set at container creation, permissions apply only to the full path, some connectors are restricted, and the page contradicts itself on Python support.

hub-and-spoke-network-topology.title: Hub-spoke network topology in Azure – Azure Architecture Center | Microsoft Learn
hub-and-spoke-network-topology.notes: Hub-and-spoke is a network pattern in which a central hub virtual network connects to many spoke virtual networks. The page describes it as the topology recommended by the Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure, in a customer-managed form; Azure Virtual WAN is the Microsoft-managed alternative. The hub holds shared services, the cross-premises gateway for VPN or ExpressRoute, egress and ingress control, and remote access to virtual machines. Spokes isolate workloads, may sit in different subscriptions and often separate production from non-production, and each is usually peered with one hub in its region. Described components include peering, Azure Bastion, Azure Firewall and VPN or ExpressRoute gateways. Typical uses are multi-environment workloads that share services such as DNS or AD DS, workloads that need central security control, and centrally managed connectivity. Peering is not transitive, so spoke-to-spoke traffic needs direct peering, Virtual Network Manager or user-defined routes through a firewall in the hub. Limits include the number of peerings per network, throughput ceilings of gateways and firewalls, SNAT port budgets, DNS consistency with the firewall, non-overlapping address spaces and scaling of hub services. No license requirements are stated.

hybrid-entra-join.title: Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices – Microsoft Learn
hybrid-entra-join.notes: Microsoft Entra hybrid join describes devices that are joined to an on-premises Windows Server Active Directory and also registered with Microsoft Entra ID. Signing in to such a device requires an organizational account. The model lets organizations with existing Active Directory use Entra ID features without replacing their directory. Devices are provisioned through domain join or Windows Autopilot. Sign-in can use passwords or passwordless methods such as Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 security keys. Devices are managed with Group Policy or Configuration Manager. Capabilities include single sign-on to cloud and on-premises resources, Conditional Access, and self-service password reset including the Windows Hello PIN reset on the lock screen. Supported systems are Windows 11 and Windows 10 except Home editions, and Windows Server 2016, 2019 and 2022. Typical scenarios are organizations that keep Group Policy or run Win32 apps that depend on Active Directory machine authentication. The main limit is that devices must regularly reach domain controllers, otherwise they become unusable; Microsoft Entra join is suggested when that dependency is a concern. No license requirements are mentioned.

illicit-consent-grant.title: Detect and remediate illicit consent grants – Microsoft Defender for Office 365
illicit-consent-grant.notes: In an illicit consent grant attack, the attacker registers an app in Microsoft Entra ID that requests access to contacts, email or documents, and then tricks a user into granting consent through phishing or injected code on a trusted site. The app then holds access tied to the user's account without needing an account in the organization. Password resets and multifactor authentication do not help, because the app sits outside the organization. Indicators include consent to application events in the audit log, the admin-consent flag set to true, suspicious or misspelled app names, and broad read, write or all permissions, especially for all principals on non-Microsoft apps. Investigation uses audit log search in the Defender portal, the Entra admin center or a PowerShell script that exports permissions. Removal uses the Entra admin center or Microsoft Graph PowerShell, and disabling the account is only a drastic stopgap. The guidance applies to Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Plan 2 and Microsoft Defender XDR, and it recommends least-privilege roles. Mailbox auditing and activity auditing must already be on before an attack to scope it. Audit entries can lag by up to a day, retention depends on licenses, and the admin center checks one user at a time.

immersive-spaces-in-teams.title: Immersive events in Microsoft Teams – Microsoft Learn
immersive-spaces-in-teams.notes: The Learn page for this topic describes Teams Immersive, which lets people create, customize and host immersive 3D events in Microsoft Teams. Events are planned in the Teams calendar, and attendees join from the Teams app on PC or Mac, or on Meta Quest 3. Organizers design 3D spaces on PC or Mac without code. The experience includes avatar movement, spatial audio, screen sharing, video and audio objects, reactions, guest participants and the use of files such as images, videos, audio and 3D models from Microsoft 365. Organizers, co-organizers and attendees need a commercial Teams license, for example Microsoft 365 or Office 365 plans that include Teams, and a global or billing admin assigns licenses. Access is managed through events policies in the Teams admin center or with a PowerShell setting. A PC or Mac needs at least a four-core CPU and 8 GB of RAM. Unsupported are Teams on the web or mobile, VDI, Teams Rooms, phone dial-in, GCC and sovereign clouds, EDU environments, and external or anonymous users; guests cannot organize. Quest has further limits such as no chat. Customization sessions expire after a period, templates cannot be reused, and the page announces that immersive events will be retired on 2 April 2027.

inactive-site-policy.title: Manage inactive sites with policies – SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
inactive-site-policy.notes: An inactive site policy detects SharePoint sites that have shown no activity for a defined period. It is set up in the SharePoint admin center as part of site lifecycle management. The policy notifies site owners or admins, asks them to confirm that a site is still needed and acts if nobody responds. Activity is judged from SharePoint, Teams, Viva Engage and Exchange signals. A policy can run in simulation mode, which runs once and produces a report, or in active mode, which runs monthly with reports, notifications and enforcement. The scope is all sites or a CSV list, and an exclusion list affects only who receives notices. Owners can certify a site, after which it is not checked for a year. After three monthly notices, the action can be nothing, read-only access, or read-only for a chosen period followed by archiving through Microsoft 365 Archive. A CSV report lists lock status, last activity, storage and action state. The page points to SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites without naming a license; custom emails need a custom domain configured. Excluded are OneDrive, root, home and app catalog sites and channel sites. Owners cannot unlock read-only sites, only tenant admins can, and disabling a policy does not undo earlier actions.

information-barriers.title: Learn about Information Barriers – Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn
information-barriers.notes: Information Barriers is a Microsoft Purview compliance solution that restricts communication and collaboration between groups and users in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive. Its purpose is to avoid conflicts of interest and protect internal information, and it is often used in highly regulated sectors. Policies define user segments, based on Microsoft Entra attributes, that may not communicate or share files with each other. Affected users cannot find, select, chat with or call one another, and automatic checks detect and block unauthorized interaction. Modes include single-segment, multi-segment and a legacy mode. In Teams the controls cover search, chats, meetings, calls and file sharing; in SharePoint and OneDrive they cover site access and sharing; in Planner the people picker hides restricted users for basic plans only. For Exchange Online, address book policies are managed by the system outside legacy mode. Example scenarios include separating traders from a marketing team and separating clients within a law firm. Compliance administrators configure the policies. Limits: only mutual restrictions are possible, email is not covered and needs mail flow rules, and legacy mode requires removing existing address book policies first. No license requirements are given.

inventory-visibility.title: Inventory Visibility add-in – Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management | Microsoft Learn
inventory-visibility.notes: The Inventory Visibility add-in is a standalone, scalable microservice for Dynamics 365 that records inventory changes and shows stock in near real time across connected data sources and channels. It provides a global view of on-hand and other quantities by site and warehouse, accepts inventory changes from external systems through APIs, and supports soft reservations that mark quantities for orders without changing physical stock, which helps prevent overselling. Available-to-promise calculations give availability and next available dates, and inventory allocation reserves stock for channels, customer groups or locations. The model uses data sources, dimensions, physical and calculated measures, partitions and an index hierarchy. Access is through REST APIs, and because data sits in Dataverse, Power Apps and Power BI can be used. The add-in is included for companies with a valid Supply Chain Management license, and a service component is included in the Intelligent Order Management bundle. Typical uses are omnichannel order fulfillment and connecting third-party order management, ERP or point-of-sale systems. Limits: calls generate Dataverse API requests that fall under service protection limits, and soft reservations and allocation were not yet available for warehouse-managed items at the time of the page.

iot-hub-device-twin.title: Understand and use device twins in IoT Hub – Microsoft Learn
iot-hub-device-twin.notes: A device twin in Azure IoT Hub is a JSON document that holds state information for a device, such as metadata, configuration and conditions. IoT Hub keeps one twin per device identity, and the twin is created and deleted together with that identity. The document has tags, which only back-end apps can read and write, desired properties, which the back end sets and the device reads, and reported properties, which the device sets and the back end can read and query. Read-only parts include version and metadata with last-updated timestamps. Typical uses are storing device metadata in the cloud, reporting connectivity state and coordinating firmware updates. Back-end apps use HTTPS with the ServiceConnect permission to fetch, update or replace twin parts and to receive change notifications, which require a route for twin change events; devices need DeviceConnect and can update reported properties and observe desired changes. The features are available in the standard tier, not in basic or free. Limits include rules for key names, value types, nesting depth and size caps for each section. Notifications for disconnected devices are not stored, reported properties only keep the latest value and update order is not guaranteed.

microsoft-ai-gateway.title: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management | Microsoft Learn
microsoft-ai-gateway.notes: The AI gateway is a group of capabilities within Azure API Management for managing AI backends such as models, agents and tools. It extends the existing API gateway rather than being a separate product, and it includes the MCP server features. Goals named on the page are authentication and authorization for AI services, load balancing across several AI endpoints, monitoring and logging of AI interactions, control of token usage and quotas across applications, and self-service for developer teams. Supported endpoints include language model APIs using the OpenAI, Anthropic Messages and Google Vertex AI schemas, remote MCP servers, A2A agent APIs and self-hosted models. Functions include a token limit policy, semantic caching for similar prompts, managed identity authentication, content safety checks, load balancing with circuit breakers, logging of prompts and completions in Azure Monitor, and token metrics. The page says the features apply to all API Management tiers, though individual feature availability depends on the tier. Semantic caching needs an external cache that supports RediSearch. The unified model API and Foundry integration are in preview, the Anthropic schema is limited to v2 tiers, and scaling the gateway does not scale the AI backends.
